title: W04b: reconciliation core operation
description: Implement the single reconciliation operation of plan 7: validate inputs, context, local object identity and task intent before planning any mutation; recover any previous intent and reload tasks, claims and history under the ledger lock; refuse duplicate target task IDs, ambiguous source filenames, invalid schemas or duplicate claim IDs affecting the target, multiple active claims, divergent lifecycle state, unsafe record paths and conflicting evidence metadata. Apply the 7.2 state table exactly, including attach-only on open tasks, the owner and claim requirement for closure, refusal for every other state and for wont_do, attach-only on done tasks, and no_change for an already-satisfied request regardless of retry actor. A close request is all-or-nothing with respect to the new intent and never partially attaches evidence. No-change writes no task, claim, timestamp, metadata or event. Resolve immutable Git data outside the lock where possible, verify a captured ledger revision before committing, and never hold the ledger lock across an unbounded subprocess. Append the 7.5 events in fixed order and return the 7.4 data contract.
acceptance: Every row of the 7.2 table is covered, including owner mismatch, non-owner closure, wont_do refusal, done with a new association requiring attach-only, and a repeated request from a different retry actor.
A failed closure attaches nothing; a successful closure updates exactly status, updated_at, closed_at and the active claim's status and completed_at.
No-change emits no writes and no events while still following recovery of a prior interrupted mutation.
Human output distinguishes attachment, closure with attachment, closure using existing evidence, and no change; JSON envelopes stay valid on failures and argument errors with nonzero exit status.
Full object and source identity, supplied hash, task source, explicit close input and outcome booleans appear in the audit events, and existing consumers tolerate the additive fields.
notes: Acceptance groups A04, A05 and A06. The existing commit-attachment helper is not idempotent and carries no source identity, so it must not be the write path; a real association is recorded in the same mutation as the commit reference.
